nodes.title: 00 North Star
nodes.description: LifeOS Planning Spine v0 turns user intent into constrained, provable execution. The system is not a general org chart, not a broad agent platform, and not a simulation playground. It is a narrow operating spine that converts an intention into a verified next action through a strict chain of authority, planning, simulation, execution, and proof.

nodes.title: 01 Object Model
nodes.description: The planning spine is built from these machine-readable entities:

nodes.title: 02 Authority Graph
nodes.description: The authority graph answers a single question: who is allowed to decide, delegate, execute, and verify each planning object.

nodes.title: 03 Task Graph Schema
nodes.description: The task graph is the executable backbone of v0. It captures ordering, authority, constraints, rollback, proof, and simulation-derived restrictions.

nodes.title: 04 WorldSeed Schema
nodes.description: `WorldSeed` is the exact simulation input package passed to DevWorld. It freezes the task context so simulation results are reproducible and can be compared across runs.

nodes.title: 05 Hermetic Cell Contract
nodes.description: The hermetic cell is the smallest runtime envelope allowed to execute a task. It exists to keep execution bounded, auditable, and rollback-aware.

nodes.title: 06 Proof Ledger
nodes.description: The proof ledger is the completion authority for the planning spine. It stores evidence that a task, action, artifact, or decision actually happened and passed its required gate.

8c. `path` lane (CLIs / plugins on PATH via the runtime closure)
8d. Audit notes (C-boundary caveats — NOT latest-wins exemptions)

nodes.title: NBV-001: REDB-CLAIM-002
nodes.description: Verify mmap/page-cache wording against pinned redb version.

metadata.required_primary_evidence: current redb source/docs for mmap and cache behavior
metadata.resolution: Current pinned redb 4.1.0 removed its mmap backend. Its optimized file backend uses positioned file reads/writes, and Database exposes a configurable userspace cache (default 1 GiB). The report's current mmap and operating-system-cache-bypass statement is false.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 100%; Node authority applied where relevant.

nodes.title: NBV-002: REDB-CLAIM-003
nodes.description: Verify zero-copy and B-tree terminology.

metadata.required_primary_evidence: redb API and on-disk encoding source
metadata.resolution: redb documents a zero-copy, BTreeMap-based API and can return borrowed views, but its Value trait explicitly serializes with as_bytes and deserializes with from_bytes. Storage uses copy-on-write B-trees, not std::collections::BTreeMap, so 'native Rust types without serialization' is too broad.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 98%; Node authority applied where relevant.

nodes.title: NBV-003: REDB-CLAIM-004
nodes.description: Verify ACID scope for the pinned version.

metadata.required_primary_evidence: redb transaction guarantees and current configuration tests
metadata.resolution: redb 4.1.0 documents full ACID transactions and serializable isolation; the complete local redb test suite passed 196 tests including immediate persistence, read isolation, transaction behavior, recovery-sensitive paths, and multithreading.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 99%; Node authority applied where relevant.

nodes.title: NBV-004: REDB-CLAIM-005
nodes.description: Verify exact reader/writer MVCC semantics.

metadata.required_primary_evidence: redb transaction concurrency implementation and tests
metadata.resolution: redb 4.1.0 documents MVCC with one writer and multiple concurrent snapshot readers; design documentation and passing concurrency tests prove readers do not block the active writer. Writer-to-writer concurrency remains serialized.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 98%; Node authority applied where relevant.

nodes.title: NBV-005: REDB-CLAIM-007
nodes.description: Prove static closure and absence of runtime Nix-store coupling.

metadata.required_primary_evidence: actual musl dependency closure and produced binaries
metadata.resolution: redb's Rust implementation is compatible with a musl/static target in principle, but portability is a whole-closure property. The active CodeDB/Yazelix binaries are dynamically linked glibc ELF files with Nix-store interpreter/RUNPATH entries, and the effective Rust toolchain lacked the musl std target, so the claimed portable closure is not currently proven.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 99%; Node authority applied where relevant.

nodes.title: NBV-006: REDB-CLAIM-008
nodes.description: Locate actual geometry/vector owner.

metadata.required_primary_evidence: code implementing vector storage, indexing, and distance calculation
metadata.resolution: redb 4.1.0 is a transactional key-value B-tree engine. It exposes no vector coordinate, geometry, nearest-neighbor, HNSW, or distance-computation API. The current Bun-loaded ruvector Node package owns vector geometry.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 100%; Node authority applied where relevant.

metadata.required_primary_evidence: cosine implementation in application or RuVector source
metadata.resolution: redb implements no cosine-similarity operation. Cosine is supplied by application or RuVector code; the Bun-loaded ruvector 0.2.34 package exports cosineSimilarity and native vector database APIs.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 99%; Node authority applied where relevant.

nodes.title: NBV-008: REDB-CLAIM-010
nodes.description: Benchmark before accepting microsecond or AVX-512 claims.

metadata.required_primary_evidence: SIMD implementation path, CPU features, dimensions, workload, and percentiles
metadata.resolution: The exact zero-copy-f32-plus-AVX-512 redb path does not exist in redb 4.1.0. A reproducible benchmark measured redb byte reads and commits plus a separate scalar application cosine loop at 384 and 4096 dimensions; microsecond results do not convert that application loop into redb functionality or prove AVX-512 use.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 100%; Node authority applied where relevant.

metadata.resolution: The local benchmark proves low redb latency on this workstation (1536-byte read p50 about 0.27 microseconds; Immediate commit p50 about 20-24 microseconds), but no claim-scoped LMDB comparator, edge-node hardware run, determinism definition, or crash/sync matrix exists. Competitive-with-LMDB remains unproved.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 92%; Node authority applied where relevant.

nodes.title: NBV-358: INGEST-CLAIM-001
nodes.description: Trace the pinned parser entry point and run a fixture corpus covering supported languages, symlinks, ignored paths, malformed files, and dependency edges.

metadata.verification_method: Trace the pinned parser entry point and run a fixture corpus covering supported languages, symlinks, ignored paths, malformed files, and dependency edges.
metadata.required_primary_evidence: Pinned source/version, AST schema, fixture outputs, deterministic workspace manifest, and failure receipts.
metadata.resolution: A narrower Rust-only implementation is proven, but the claim is materially overbroad and assigns ownership imprecisely. At nu_plugin commit 9451b20e42d79f72d4fa5b2a190a39bd1d9d5e5a, Nushell is the plugin host/table cockpit; Rust code recursively enumerates the selected root, selects files classified as Rust source, reads them as UTF-8, parses them with syn, and emits syntax-only rows including functions and structs. Cargo dependency rows are obtained separately by invoking `cargo metadata --format-version 1`, not mapped from the Rust AST. The active profile-owned CodeDB 0.1.0 binary reproduced the function/struct rows and captured real symlink metadata, but it also traversed `.git` (437 rows) and `target` (13,738 rows), so ignored/generated boundaries are classified rather than excluded. Polyglot AST support remains documented as candidates/planning, not current implementation. The complete required fixture corpus was not executable under the strict no-write constraint because there is no committed malformed-Rust fixture and the dependency fixture has no Cargo.lock while the product's metadata command lacks `--locked`; therefore the exact broad claim is qualified, not verified.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11; confidence 96%; meta-ruvector not-used.

nodes.title: NBV-359: INGEST-CLAIM-002
nodes.description: Trace plugin output into the pinned redb writer and replay ordered, duplicate, malformed, interrupted, and concurrent block fixtures.

metadata.verification_method: Trace plugin output into the pinned redb writer and replay ordered, duplicate, malformed, interrupted, and concurrent block fixtures.
metadata.required_primary_evidence: Local call-path trace, schema/version receipt, transaction tests, crash/replay evidence, and exact record hashes.
metadata.resolution: Current primary evidence contradicts the exact implementation claim. The current nu_plugin_codedb surface declares Type::Nothing input, every inspected command run method ignores `_input`, and the plugin crate has no codedb-store-redb/redb dependency; it produces native Nushell table values from repository/path arguments instead of receiving structured blocks. The pinned redb 4.1.0 writer exists in a separate codedb CLI path and persists `(relative_path, bytes)` batches scanned from the filesystem. Existing redb tests cover durable byte batches, checkpoint resume, future-schema refusal, and writer contention, but there is no plugin-output-to-redb call path or structured-block schema to replay. Installed profile ownership also keeps separate `codedb` and `nu_plugin_codedb` binaries; binary probes found redb writer symbols only in `codedb`, while the plugin contains the explicit text `redb store is not implemented until CDB015`. No write-producing fixture/test command was run because this pass was strictly read-only.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11; confidence 98%; meta-ruvector reference-only.

nodes.title: NBV-360: INGEST-CLAIM-003
nodes.description: Trace a bounded redb-to-PostgreSQL run with pinned embedding configuration, selected source identity, transaction receipt, and repeat/recovery tests.

metadata.verification_method: Trace a bounded redb-to-PostgreSQL run with pinned embedding configuration, selected source identity, transaction receipt, and repeat/recovery tests.
metadata.required_primary_evidence: Pinned envctl and embedding inputs, selected-record manifest, PostgreSQL transaction/row receipt, vector dimension/hash receipt, and recovery proof.
metadata.resolution: Current primary evidence contradicts the asserted envctl pipeline. Envctl's contract forbids reading CodeDB redb internals; its default-off semantic module reads exported JSONL rows that already contain embedding_minilm vectors and builds only an in-memory HNSW index. No tracked caller of SemanticIndex was found. Envctl's ruvector-postgres dependency is an optional, default-off server-side extension, explicitly not a PostgreSQL client. A separate CodeDB implementation in the nu_plugin repository can capture raw file bytes directly to either redb or PostgreSQL through alternative BlobStore backends, but its PostgreSQL table explicitly omits the optional embedding column and its parity test independently writes the same fixture to both stores rather than transferring redb blocks to PostgreSQL. No envctl redb-to-PostgreSQL call path, embedding-generation owner/model, transaction receipt, or repeat/recovery run exists in the inspected evidence. Installed behavior was not proven: envctl is absent from PATH and from /home/flexnetos/.nix-profile/bin; only a source-build symlink exists under /home/flexnetos/meta/usr/bin, which is not an active profile frontdoor.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11; confidence 97%; meta-ruvector not-used.

nodes.title: NBV-361: INGEST-CLAIM-004
nodes.description: Reconcile the three stages against the committed task graph and define stage-level contracts and gates.

metadata.verification_method: Reconcile the three stages against the committed task graph and define stage-level contracts and gates.
metadata.required_primary_evidence: Owner-reviewed pipeline graph, stage contracts, fixture-based end-to-end proof, and explicit acceptance decision.
metadata.resolution: The core statement is proven only as captured source framing: NBSOURCE-030 presents parser, redb buffer, and redb-to-PostgreSQL bridge atoms and summarizes them as a Phase 1 three-step flat-file-to-database proposal. It is not yet a committed, accepted, or implemented pipeline. Reconciliation against the committed graph is: (1) flat files -> AST blocks: FOUNDATION-001 must pin the sole parser/runtime package owner and POSTGRES-004 must define a read-only, bounded collector with stable source identity, byte/metadata hashes, AST schema, provenance, ordering, checkpoints, failure recovery, and lossless reconstruction; gate on a pinned parser plus deterministic fixture corpus and failure receipts. (2) AST blocks -> redb staging: require a versioned block schema, exact record hashes, ordered/idempotent writes, deduplication, crash replay, recovery source, and an explicit transient-versus-durable authority decision; gate on ordered/duplicate/malformed/interrupted/concurrent fixtures and STORE-001/PGAUTH-002 owner approval. This stage is not adequately represented by the claim's four aggregate refs and instead appears in adjacent draft tasks PGAUTH-002, POSTGRES-006, STORE-001, and the INGEST-CLAIM-002 queue row. (3) redb -> embedded PostgreSQL: require selected-record identity, pinned embedding model/configuration, transactional row/vector receipts, provenance, repeat/recovery behavior, and one-way authority into PostgreSQL; gate on a bounded transaction test, vector dimension/hash receipts, and deterministic round-trip projection. POSTGRES-008 is specifically the reverse database-to-directory projection contract, not the forward ingestion bridge, so POSTGRES-005/006/009 and PGAUTH-004 are also needed for the complete bridge/round-trip. Final gate: owner-reviewed pipeline graph, committed stage contracts, fixture-based end-to-end proof, explicit acceptance, then LIFEOS-011 only after all child proofs pass. All four canonical aggregate tasks are currently Draft and their planned artifacts/proofs are absent.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11; confidence 96%; meta-ruvector not-used.

nodes.title: NBV-362: INGEST-CLAIM-005
nodes.description: Define source identity, record schema, ordering, byte preservation, and projection/round-trip acceptance before treating the proposal as implementable.

metadata.verification_method: Define source identity, record schema, ordering, byte preservation, and projection/round-trip acceptance before treating the proposal as implementable.
metadata.required_primary_evidence: Canonical source manifest, schema and migration receipt, deterministic round trip, and owner-approved authority matrix.
metadata.resolution: Current local canonical records support the narrow statement that NBSOURCE-030 was captured and normalized as proposing a flat-file-to-database-hosted codebase representation. They do not establish that the proposal is implementable. The canonical claim row explicitly calls it a source-only proposal without a canonical file manifest, byte-level round trip, or ownership decision; the verification row remains queued; all four referenced implementation/policy tasks are Draft; and every named task-family, plan, acceptance, and proof artifact for POSTGRES-004, POSTGRES-008, POSTGRES-009, and PGAUTH-004 is absent. In addition, the exact 810-byte source fulltext is identified and hashed but not retained in the inspected workspace, so the semantic wording is independently evidenced only through the canonical normalized capture, not through locally reviewable raw source text.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11; confidence 96%; meta-ruvector not-used.

nodes.title: NBV-363: PERF-CLAIM-001
nodes.description: Benchmark the exact plugin-to-redb operation with fixed payloads, warm/cold state, sync mode, concurrency, percentile targets, and failure injection.

metadata.verification_method: Benchmark the exact plugin-to-redb operation with fixed payloads, warm/cold state, sync mode, concurrency, percentile targets, and failure injection.
metadata.required_primary_evidence: Versioned benchmark harness, raw distributions, environment manifest, durability semantics, and independently repeatable results.
metadata.resolution: Refuted as a claim about the current or installed implementation. At nu_plugin HEAD 9451b20 and at the Yazelix-locked installed-source revision 532a461, nu_plugin_codedb has no codedb-store-redb/redb dependency and its scan/import commands return Nushell rows; the source and tests characterize the plugin surface as read-only. A real durable redb write exists, but in the separate codedb CLI/codedb_store_redb path, where persist_batch performs the transaction and commit. No benchmark target, benchmark dependency, percentile metric, warm/cold protocol, sync-mode matrix, concurrency matrix, or failure-injection latency result exists. Thus there is neither an exact plugin-to-redb operation nor primary benchmark evidence supporting microsecond latency.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11; confidence 98%; meta-ruvector not-used.

nodes.title: NBV-364: AUTH-CLAIM-001
nodes.description: Produce an authority matrix and authorized/denied write traces for file, redb, envctl, embedding, and PostgreSQL layers.

metadata.verification_method: Produce an authority matrix and authorized/denied write traces for file, redb, envctl, embedding, and PostgreSQL layers.
metadata.required_primary_evidence: Committed authority policy, identity/version receipts, transaction authorization traces, conflict/rollback tests, and owner approval.
metadata.resolution:
The exact authority claim is refuted by current local primary evidence. PostgreSQL is an implemented optional direct CodeDB backend, but envctl is not the synchronizing writer in that path: CodeDB selects either redb (the default durable backend) or PostgreSQL and calls the selected backend's persist_batch directly. The PostgreSQL implementation performs its own INSERT/ON CONFLICT transaction into the dedicated codebase_codedb table and deliberately avoids the production codebase table. Envctl manages the PostgreSQL/RuVector component lifecycle and consumes already-embedded CodeDB export rows into an in-memory index; the inspected envctl path neither generates those embeddings nor writes ingested blocks/embeddings to PostgreSQL. The planning graph expresses a future PostgreSQL macro-authority/projection design, but every canonical task cited by this claim is Draft, the required authority artifacts are absent, and the claim queue remains queued with Ready empty.

Authority matrix (current evidence):

CodeDB export rows that name envctl as a possible materialization owner are declarative (`runtime_status=declared`) and have no current envctl consumer. Relevant tracked source files had empty diffs. metadata.resolution: redb is an in-process single-node embedded store and exposes no network server, replication protocol, or distributed-consensus API. Distribution therefore belongs to application protocols.

metadata.resolution: redb is key-value and has no SQL or automatic relational secondary-index facility. Qualification is required because it supports named tables, range scans, and multimap tables from which an application can explicitly build indexes.
metadata.notes: Local primary truth pass 2026-07-11T10:29:30Z; confidence 98%; Node authority applied where relevant.
